result:
If there were a single lever to alter the trajectory of human history, it would be to grant every person the temporary, vivid ability to experience the world through the mind of another—to truly feel their pain, their joy, their fears, and their history.

So much of human suffering is not a design flaw of the physical universe, but a product of cognitive isolation. We are trapped inside our own skulls, guessing at the internal lives of others, which makes it easy to misunderstand, fear, and dehumanize. 

If we could close that gap—even for a moment—the foundations of cruelty, conflict, and systemic indifference would erode. It would not erase our differences, but it would make apathy impossible. That shift in perspective is the most powerful catalyst for everything else: genuine cooperation, shared progress, and peace.
